policy.selection: Pick the lowest priority ready item, then prefer product value and smallest safe implementation slice.
policy.agent_rule: Agent findings must be converted into backlog items before execution.
policy.execution_loop: read GOAL.md -> read docs/backlog.json -> scripts/backlog.py goal -> implement one highest-priority unblocked task -> test -> run scripts/ui_smoke.py for UI changes -> update backlog and DEVELOPMENT_LOG -> rebuild exe/installer for product changes -> commit -> push
policy.release_goal: LumaSift v0.1 is a local-first graphical AI photo curation product ready for friend testing and public demonstration, not a CLI demo.

items.title: Establish executable backlog loop
items.rationale: Planning-agent findings were not automatically becoming execution work. The repo needs a durable source of truth for the agent loop.
acceptance: docs/BACKLOG.md explains the operating loop.
docs/backlog.json contains prioritized executable work.
scripts/backlog.py can show the next ready item.
Development log records the new workflow.
items.risk: If this remains only conversational, planning reviews will keep drifting away from implementation.

items.title: Virtualized thumbnail grid MVP
items.rationale: The current item-based review grid will struggle with thousands of photos.
acceptance: Load 2000+ result records without creating heavyweight widgets for every row.
Scrolling remains responsive.
Only visible cells and a small prefetch window request thumbnail work.
Search, sorting, filtering, selection, and labels still work.
Thumbnail loading remains cancellable.
items.risk: Model/view refactor can break selection, detail panel, and label persistence.

items.title: Stabilize selection and label state after grid virtualization
items.rationale: Virtualized cells must not leak stale labels, thumbnails, or selection state.
acceptance: Keep/maybe/reject display correctly in virtualized cells.
Multi-select and batch marking work after filtering and sorting.
Label filters all/keep/maybe/reject/unlabeled work.
Labels restore after rerun or app restart.
items.risk: Cell reuse can show stale visual state unless data roles are authoritative.

items.title: Qwen analysis queue UI
items.rationale: Users need to see where time and API spend are going during Top-N vision review.
acceptance: UI shows queued/running/done/cache-hit/failed/retrying states.
UI shows current model, Top-N, completed count, failed count, and cache hits.
Local progress and Qwen progress are separate.
Failures are readable and reports remain usable.
items.risk: Current harness exposes only coarse progress; richer events are needed.

items.title: Qwen queue cancellation and graceful downgrade
items.rationale: A commercial local app must let users stop expensive/slow API work without losing local results, but this should follow the current Chinese-first GUI and 200+ photo release baseline so cancellation work is integrated into a stable main workflow.
acceptance: User can cancel only the Qwen stage without discarding completed local ranking results.
Completed Qwen items remain saved and visible in the queue/report state.
Pending Qwen items become skipped/cancelled with readable Chinese and English UI status.
In-flight network work stops safely where supported; otherwise the UI enters a cancelling state and prevents duplicate submissions.
Qwen queue strip updates cancelled/skipped state separately from failed/retrying/cache-hit/done counts.
Report still contains local-only ranking plus Qwen done/cache-hit/failed/cancelled status.
Cancellation does not corrupt Qwen cache writes or saved labels.
python scripts/ui_smoke.py covers the cancelled/downgraded visual state without requiring a live API key.
items.risk: Network request cancellation and cache writes need conservative handling.

items.title: Retire SQLite run history view
items.rationale: The in-app history page added navigation and state-management weight without helping the current analysis-and-advice workflow.
acceptance: The desktop top navigation no longer exposes a History page.
Review mode no longer shows a history/restore action.
Run-history persistence and restore code are removed from the app and tests.
SQLite photo labels, manifest reuse, preview paths, and Qwen cache linkage remain available.
items.risk: Users who want to revisit an old result now use exported report/contact-sheet files from the output folder.

items.title: Unify SQLite manifest and cache identity
items.rationale: A persistent photo manifest enables faster reruns and less repeated API spend.
acceptance: Each photo stores path, size, mtime, identity hash, preview path, last_run_id, scores, and Qwen cache key.
Reruns only recompute changed files where safe.
JSON/CSV remain export formats rather than the sole state store.
items.risk: Schema migration, path case, external drives, and moved folders add complexity.

items.title: Use keep/maybe/reject as review feedback without polluting model score
items.rationale: User labels should improve workflow while remaining separable from algorithm scores.
acceptance: Keep items can be prioritized or surfaced in future runs.
Reject items can skip repeated Qwen review unless explicitly enabled.
Reports distinguish user_label from model score/category.
items.risk: User preference and model evaluation must not be conflated.

items.title: Evaluation dataset format
items.rationale: A labeled local evaluation set is required to prove ranking quality.
acceptance: Define local eval labels format with photo path/id, gold label, story rank, notes, split, and prompt version.
Export from SQLite labels without copying private photos into git.
Document a 100-300 photo evaluation workflow.
items.risk: Private photo paths and data must not be committed.

items.title: Ranking evaluation metrics tool
items.rationale: Precision@K/NDCG@K make the AI ranking system measurable rather than anecdotal.
acceptance: Compute Precision@K, Recall@K, NDCG@K, MRR, and label distribution.
Compare local-only and Qwen runs by prompt_version/model_version.
Write metrics JSON and Markdown summary.
items.risk: Small subjective datasets can produce unstable metrics.

items.title: Qwen prompt version evaluation loop
items.rationale: Prompt changes must be comparable and cache-safe.
acceptance: Prompt version appears in Qwen cache key and reports.
Evaluation report can compare prompt A/B.
Report lists false negatives such as technically weak but story-strong photos.
items.risk: Model version drift and API cost can reduce comparability.

items.title: Windows installer signing
items.rationale: Signing matters for commercial distribution but should follow core workflow stability.
acceptance: Build script supports optional Authenticode certificate path or CI secret.
Unsigned friend-test build still works.
Document certificate options and timestamping.
items.risk: Certificate cost, timestamp service failures, and secret handling.

items.title: Versioned release and auto-update plan
items.rationale: Auto-update is commercial hardening, not a core selection workflow feature.
acceptance: App version, installer version, portable zip version, and release notes are consistent.
Document update channel strategy.
Choose Inno/MSIX/Squirrel/winget-style path.
items.risk: Windows auto-update can trigger permissions and antivirus issues.

items.title: Crash diagnostics and privacy-safe log export
items.rationale: Friend testing and early product use need actionable bug reports without leaking photos or keys.
acceptance: GUI can open logs folder.
GUI can export a diagnostics bundle with version, run summary, events, and tracebacks.
Bundle excludes API keys and original photos.
items.risk: Privacy filtering must be reliable.

items.title: Friend-test observability checklist
items.rationale: A repeatable test matrix makes the product safer to send to friends.
acceptance: Friend-test guide covers 100/500/2000 photo runs.
Guide covers local/Qwen, cancel, cache hit, labels, output review, and reinstall.
Expected results match current GUI behavior.
items.risk: Docs can drift from implementation.

items.title: Similar-photo grouping and best-of-group selection
items.rationale: Real culling often means choosing the strongest image from near-duplicates and burst-like sequences.
acceptance: Group visually similar photos using perceptual hash or embeddings.
Show group size and best candidate.
Qwen can be applied to group winners instead of every similar frame.
items.risk: Weak similarity grouping can accidentally hide meaningful differences.

items.title: Top-K explainable selection report
items.rationale: Users need a clear explanation of why the top images are worth editing.
acceptance: Top-K report explains keep reasons, reject risks, editing potential, and final ordering.
Report highlights story-strong but technically imperfect photos.
Report can be viewed from the GUI and exported.
items.risk: Report quality depends on Qwen reliability and structured output quality.

items.title: Formalize v0.1 GOAL and UI smoke gate
items.rationale: The product needs a durable release goal and a mandatory automated UI smoke loop so UI regressions are caught before the user has to screenshot them.
acceptance: GOAL.md defines LumaSift v0.1 as a release-oriented local-first graphical product.
docs/BACKLOG.md defines the 继续 goal execution loop.
docs/backlog.json records the v0.1 product policy.
scripts/ui_smoke.py generates setup and review screenshots.
scripts/ui_smoke.py writes JSON and Markdown reports and exits nonzero on layout failures.
Tests cover the UI smoke script.
items.risk: If the goal remains only conversational, future iterations can regress into demo work or miss visual defects.

items.title: 200+ RAW GUI release stability run
items.rationale: The v0.1 product target is a local graphical desktop app. The release gate should validate the current Chinese-first GUI after the latest review cockpit, label, Qwen queue, and UI smoke changes.
acceptance: Run the current desktop GUI against a 200+ real RAW/JPG folder in local-only mode without committing private photos or generated outputs.
The app remains responsive enough to review results after the run and shuts down cleanly without QThread or worker lifecycle crashes.
Review board, detail cockpit, large preview, keep/maybe/reject labels, label filters, and selected-photo editing advice remain usable after the 200+ photo run.
Record runtime, processed count, failure count, memory-risk observations, and output artifact locations in DEVELOPMENT_LOG using privacy-safe wording.
Run python scripts/ui_smoke.py after any fix made during this task and inspect the generated report/screenshots before marking done.
items.risk: The already-passing CLI/local harness can hide GUI-specific thread, thumbnail, layout, and state-restoration failures.

items.title: Release-readiness checklist and friend-test flow
items.rationale: A friend-testable product needs a clear installation and first-run flow, not just a generated installer.
acceptance: Document installer path, first-run workflow, Qwen key setup, privacy behavior, and expected outputs.
Add a friend-test checklist covering install, import, local analysis, Qwen Top-N, labels, editing plan, and output opening.
Record known limitations and safe recovery steps.
items.risk: Users can fail the product through unclear onboarding even when the core code works.

items.title: Constructivist review cockpit and Chinese local fallback
items.rationale: The right review panel was visually unbalanced and still exposed English fallback text in a Chinese-first product.
acceptance: Review cockpit has a wider stable panel and no horizontal text overflow.
Chinese local-only detail output does not show English fallback strings.
Constructivist visual guidance is introduced through high-contrast rails and color hierarchy.
UI smoke checks the review/detail panel width and local fallback language.
items.risk: Aggressive visual language can reduce readability unless it is constrained to rails, emphasis, and action hierarchy.

items.title: Chinese-first friend-test main workflow rehearsal
items.rationale: Friend-testable v0.1 needs the visible Chinese-first graphical workflow to feel complete before adding more Qwen behavior.
acceptance: Starting from a fresh app launch, a Chinese-default user can choose a folder, run analysis, enter review mode, inspect a large preview, mark keep/maybe/reject, generate selected-photo editing advice, and find exported outputs without reading implementation details.
No English fallback strings appear in the Chinese default path for local-only review details, labels, categories, editing advice headings, or status messages.
The first screen and review mode use state, layout, and controls to guide action without adding long explanatory text.
Missing Qwen API key or local-only mode presents a clear non-blocking state and does not make the product look broken.
Run python scripts/ui_smoke.py and inspect setup, expanded setup, review, and editing-plan screenshots for clipping, overlap, wrong language, or unusable control compression.
items.risk: A technically working app can still fail friend testing if the visible Chinese workflow feels unfinished, confusing, or inconsistent.

items.title: Chinese glyph and graphic control smoke gate
items.rationale: The previous UI smoke passed while screenshots showed unreadable Chinese glyph boxes and text-heavy state controls.
acceptance: The desktop app explicitly selects a Chinese-capable UI font on Windows and registers Microsoft YaHei font files for offscreen smoke rendering.
Chinese UI smoke fails when required Chinese and decision glyphs cannot render.
Qwen queue state is rendered as compact graphic status chips instead of a long log-style sentence.
Review action controls use graphic decision buttons and icon-only output controls with tooltips.
UI smoke checks decision-button dimensions, icon-only controls, compact Qwen state, and source file state.
items.risk: Symbol-only controls must use glyphs covered by the selected font or stable Qt standard icons.

items.title: Stabilize review cockpit scrolling and Qwen story prompt v2
items.rationale: After Top-N review, the right cockpit could repaint incorrectly during mouse-wheel scrolling, and the analysis text was too generic for story-first street/documentary selection.
acceptance: Right cockpit detail scrolling remains visually stable and keeps the action controls usable.
UI smoke includes a scrolled-detail screenshot and checks right-panel/action-button stability.
Qwen prompt requires concrete visible evidence, subject relationship, decisive moment read, and why-this-frame judgment.
Qwen response merge, GUI detail, CSV, and contact sheet preserve the new story-evidence fields.
Local-only fallback clearly presents itself as technical pre-screening and varies reasons by image metrics.
A live Qwen smoke confirms the v2 prompt returns concrete visible evidence instead of generic photo-review phrasing.
items.risk: Prompt quality still needs larger human-labeled evaluation, but v2 prevents the most obvious generic analysis failure.

items.title: Photographer-grade story reading and evidence-bound editing advice
items.rationale: The selected editing advice still flattened Qwen evidence into template-like Lightroom text, making the product sound generic instead of like a serious street/documentary photo editor.
acceptance: Qwen prompt v3 requests visible inventory, editorial verdict, score rationales, moment status, frame failure reasons, and evidence-bound editing plan.
Local-only records are marked as local technical pre-screening and as needing Qwen review.
Selected editing advice separates formal vision-evidence advice from technical drafts and blocks unsupported photographic claims.
GUI and Markdown advice show photo reading, visible evidence, content decision, crop keep/reduce reasoning, local mask targets, and do-not-overedit guidance.
UI smoke fails if the advice page loses visible evidence, crop reasoning, do-not-overedit guidance, or reintroduces generic subject-relationship claims.
A live Qwen v3 smoke on private local RAW files returns concrete evidence and structured editing actions rather than generic review text.
items.risk: Top-N runs must include enough Qwen-reviewed records; local-only review is now intentionally framed as pre-screening, not final photographic judgment.

items.title: Qwen activation guardrails and no-silent-local fallback
items.rationale: A user can configure Qwen keys but still accidentally run local-only mode, producing no deep analysis without a clear explanation.
acceptance: Typing or pasting a Qwen key in the GUI switches the mode to Qwen review.
The key field remains editable even while the mode is local.
When keys exist but mode is local, the GUI shows a visible warning that the current run will not perform deep review.
Starting a local run with configured keys asks whether to switch to Qwen Top-N review instead of silently running local-only.
Desktop tests cover key-entry promotion and local-mode warning visibility.
items.risk: The confirmation dialog should prevent accidental API spend while still making Qwen activation obvious.

items.title: Compact top navigation and Qwen key quota check
items.rationale: The first screen still wasted vertical space on a hero area, setup controls crowded the review board, and Qwen failures showed only a count without key/quota diagnostics.
acceptance: The oversized hero is replaced by a compact top navigation bar with language, settings, and run stats.
The workflow strip sits near the top of the app instead of below a decorative header.
The setup/run panel can be folded from the top navigation.
Qwen API keys can be checked from the GUI and return validity plus remaining quota.
Qwen queue failures expose the latest provider error through the UI instead of only showing a failed count.
UI smoke and desktop click-path tests cover the compact navigation and settings toggle.
items.risk: A full Lightroom-style multi-page settings workspace is still larger than this v0.1 slice, but the current panel can now be hidden without losing the main review workflow.

items.title: VSCode-style compact nav and full settings workspace
items.rationale: The compact navigation still carried decorative branding and summary cards, and the settings area still had a nested advanced toggle that made the setup surface feel like a cramped form instead of a professional software workspace.
acceptance: The visible LumaSift wordmark and permanent scanned/shown/selected/mode cards are removed from the desktop canvas.
The top navigation uses a low-height VSCode-like menu strip with language switching preserved.
Opening settings shows all run, Qwen, key-check, and output controls directly without an advanced expand/collapse path.
The visual system moves toward sharper constructivist geometry with low-radius panels and hard color rails.
Review decision and output controls use compact geometric/icon controls with tooltips instead of large text-heavy buttons.
Desktop regression tests and UI smoke cover the always-expanded settings workspace and compact review action strip.
items.risk: Icon-only controls rely on stable tooltips and recognizable symbols; friend testing should confirm the glyph vocabulary is understood.

items.title: Independent workbench/settings pages and Qwen progress feedback
items.rationale: The nav still mixed commands with pages, settings overlapped the review surface, Qwen deep review lacked a clear progress affordance, and cancel reused close handling in a way that could make the app appear to exit.
acceptance: The top nav exposes independent View, Settings, Shortcuts, and Help pages, with View placed before Settings.
Run and Cancel are workbench controls, while Run and Output are removed from the navigation bar.
The Settings page is independent and fully expanded instead of sharing space with the review board.
Qwen deep review shows a determinate progress bar, model name, queue counts, current file state, and a short observable pipeline status.
Cancel writes the stop file and pauses analysis without setting the window into pending-close mode.
UI smoke captures the main page, settings page, Qwen progress panel, review board, scrolled cockpit, and editing plan.
items.risk: The current Qwen status can expose only observable pipeline phases, not hidden model chain-of-thought; live API cancellation still stops between candidates unless the provider request returns earlier.

items.title: Scene-sequence grouping and photographer-grade editing parameters
items.rationale: Near-duplicate grouping alone split real street/documentary sequences, while deep-review output still leaked raw English Lightroom keys and lacked color-grading structure.
acceptance: Similar grouping uses an additional scene signature and filename-sequence guard so visually related consecutive frames can form one group without merging unrelated distant files.
Non-best group members are skipped by Qwen by default, with only user-selected, very close, or story/decisive-moment-risk alternates preserved for deep review.
Records and CSV manifest carry scene signature and group review role fields without changing model scores.
Selected editing advice includes basic, curve, HSL/color mixer, color grading, calibration, detail, noise reduction, lens correction, and grain/vignette parameters.
Chinese UI and Markdown show professional Chinese parameter names instead of raw English parameter keys.
Qwen key checking reports the automatically selected vision model and stores it for subsequent runs.
UI smoke checks the Chinese color-grading parameter surface and prevents raw English parameter keys from leaking into Chinese editing plans.
items.risk: Scene grouping remains conservative and should keep evolving with real photographer feedback so decisive moments are not hidden.
